rules.title: California application screening fee cap
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge a rental applicant a screening fee only up to the actual out-of-pocket cost of gathering information about the applicant. The fee may not exceed $30 per applicant, adjusted annually for CPI since January 1, 1998. The landlord must refund any part of the fee not used for a reference check or credit report.
rules.key_value: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted annually from 1998-01-01; capped at actual out-of-pocket cost
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords (owners of residential rental property) or their agents who receive a request to rent a residential unit. Applies to applicants and to guarantors/cosigners.
rules.exemptions: Does not preempt deposit/fee rules under federal or state housing assistance programs.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.
rules.conflict_note: The document does not state an effective date for the statute; CPI adjustment begins January 1, 1998. The current CPI-adjusted dollar amount is not stated.

rules.title: California screening fee conditions: unit availability and first-come or refund process
rules.requirement: A landlord may not charge a screening fee when no unit is or will soon be available. A fee may be charged only if the landlord offers one of two processes. The first is a first-come, first-served review using written screening criteria, charging only applicants actually considered and refunding inadvertent fees within 7 days. The second is a full refund to every unselected applicant within 7 days of selection or 30 days of application, whichever comes first.
rules.key_value: Refund within 7 days of selection or 30 days of submission, whichever first (alternative process)
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords or their agents charging application screening fees for residential rental property in California.

rules.title: California screening fee receipt and credit report copy requirement
rules.requirement: A landlord who collects a screening fee must give the applicant an itemized receipt of out-of-pocket expenses and time spent. The landlord must also provide a copy of the consumer credit report within seven days of receiving it.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords or their agents who collect an application screening fee for residential rental property.
rules.quoted_span: If an application screening fee has been paid by the applicant, the landlord or their agent shall provide a copy of the consumer credit report to the applicant who is the subject of that report by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days of the landlord or their agent receiving the report.
